no_loosening.method: every attempt's answer from both arms, validated by the base commit's SelectionPlan and by the candidate's

not_covered: Whether the right plan finds the right photograph: retrieval, the text join and the packet are not exercised. Only the plan is scored.
The plan's limit is not scored, so a right plan with a null query and a limit of one may still hand the composer the wrong photograph at a place with several.
The composer and the answer a person reads.
Any model but the structured-extraction primary, any language but English, and catalogues larger than eleven entities.
Questions naming a place that is not saved, or naming two places.
Real personal data: every name is invented.

candidate_change: exulanica/models/client.py: a refusal from ModelClient.structured names every reason the schema class gave, with its location, and quotes the answer to 1000 characters. It used to keep a count of errors and 300 characters, which on the planner's pretty-printed plan stopped before the refused field, and the planner's one repair sends that refusal back to the model.

exulanica/selection/plan.py: the content selection's two refusals name the field and say that a search for anything visible or written in photographs is a captures or entities selection. What SelectionPlan accepts is unchanged; no_loosening measures that.

exulanica/selection/question.py, PROMPT_VERSION selection-6: the intent rules say a question about a named place is captures or entities with the place in place, and that content is never the answer to a question about anything visible or written; an id is only for what the question names; two examples show a framing verb dropped and a query left null. The query rule keeps its words 'content terms'.

development_versions.note: Five versions were tried on the development split only, 5 draws of each of its 20 questions. v1 and v2 reworded the query rule away from 'content terms' and let the question's own verb into the query ('sign say'); v3 restored the rule and its place intent clause made place questions fill a query they did not have; v4 and v5 are the line that was frozen.

deviations: The pre-registration excludes provider errors from the rates and did not anticipate a truncated reply. A truncated reply is the model's failure, so it is counted as a failed draw, which can only lower the candidate's rate. Under the literal exclusion the candidate's place rate would be 57 of 58.

The no_loosening comparison first reported a disagreement on every accepted answer. The base commit's plan module had been loaded without registering it, so Pydantic could not resolve its annotations and it refused everything. This was found before the record was written and fixed. The comparison is now guarded by a control that each class must pass, accepting a right plan and refusing a content plan with a semantic query; with the registration removed, the writer stops at the control.
findings: H-P08: in 2 of 5 candidate draws the model wrote a correct content plan up to its scope and then emitted whitespace until the 2048-token limit, and the client raised TruncatedResponseError. answer_question does not catch that error from the planner, so the product would fail the question rather than answer it. Across every candidate draw of a question whose right intent is content, development and held-out together, it happened 2 times in 35; the baseline did not do it in its 15. Counted here as failed draws.

H-H01, 'Which photographs show Ottilie Brandt?': the candidate wrote the redacted name without its brackets ('person a') as the semantic query in 4 of 5 draws; the placeholder scrub removes only the bracketed form. The baseline left the query null in 5 of 5. The text dimension is an inner join, so that query keeps only the person's photographs whose text says 'person'. A per-question regression that the aggregate person gate does not show, because H-H08 moved from 0 of 5 to 5 of 5.
H-H04: one candidate draw kept the verb 'say' in the query.

H-P05, 'Who was I with at Ashgrove Orchard?': the baseline named all four people in the catalogue with mode together in 3 of 5 draws, and in the other 2 put the place id in the entity selector instead of the place selector. That selects the same photographs, and the pre-registered scorer counts it wrong; counted as right, the baseline's place rate would be 22 of 60. The candidate named nobody in any draw.

H-H08, 'Where have I photographed Priya?': in 4 of 5 draws the baseline named no entity and wrote the redacted name without brackets into the query ('photographed person A'), and the fifth was refused; the candidate named Priya's entity with no query in 5 of 5. So the unbracketed placeholder in a query is not new with the candidate: on the baseline it appears on this question, on the candidate on H-H01.
notes.latency_note: Wall milliseconds on a shared machine, niceness 0 on every run, one-minute load average between 4.03 and 15.61 across the ten runs, arms alternated so both saw the same conditions.
notes.what_follows: The two regressions above are fixed in a second change and measured on a fresh held-out split under its own pre-registration, which binds this record as its predecessor.

record.profile_note: Outcome of the pre-registered planner reliability experiment, scored once per arm on the held-out split. No model call is made to write it.
